deals.headline: Rogers buys Kilmer's remaining 25% of MLSE, becomes sole owner

deals.summary: Rogers acquired BCE's 37.5% stake in MLSE, becoming majority owner with 75%; agreement announced in 2024, closed in 2025.

notes: Country corrected to Canada. Toronto FC publishes no accounts (a division of MLSE); revenue and operating income are Forbes estimates. The Forbes team page gives 2024-25 revenue $69M / operating income -$12M; Forbes' separate MLS list of 13 Feb 2026 (forbes.com, 403 to scripts, read via a verbatim mirror) gives #13, $725 million, revenue $74 million, operating income -$14 million for 2025 with 'One-Year Change: 0%' - not stored to keep the verifiable page. Forbes team page still names Bell Canada and Tanenbaum as owners (stale). BMO Field capacity: CBC says 'close to 30,000', BMO Field history page mentions a capacity crowd of 'more than 28,000' (2007); no exact current figure stated, so null (the earlier record's 28,351 came from Wikipedia and was dropped; Forbes' '22,000' looks wrong and was not used). Stadium built 2007 at $62.9 million and expanded 2014-15 ($120 million undertaking) per bmofield.com history. Rogers first bought into MLSE in 2012 (with Bell, from Ontario Teachers') - before 2015, no deal row. Chair, shirt sponsor (BMO), kit supplier (adidas), attendance and social counts not confirmed on a citable page.

owners.evidence: increasing its ownership of MLSE to 100%
owners.name: Rogers Communications Inc. (via Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment)

ownership_summary: Toronto FC is part of Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment (MLSE), wholly owned by Rogers Communications (TSX/NYSE-listed) since 1 October 2026, when Rogers bought Kilmer Sports Inc.'s (Larry Tanenbaum) remaining 25% for C$4.35bn. Rogers had become 75% owner in July 2025 by buying BCE's 37.5% for C$4.7bn. Rogers has said it plans to sell minority stakes in its combined sports and media portfolio to other investors by the first half of 2027.
